small_guidance:
- The inner loop order is `kh, kw, ic` with `ic` as the slowest — swap to `ic, kh, kw` (or use `tl.static_range` over `kh,kw` and a vectorized `ic` block load) so that the accumulator reuses x_val/w_val across the small static spatial dims and the IC reduction can be done with `tl.dot`. Loading x as `[BLOCK_IC, BLOCK_SP]` and w as `[BLOCK_OC, BLOCK_IC]` and calling `tl.dot` will be far faster than the current scalar-outer-product over IC=16.
- Add autotune configs with `BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_SP=32/64` plus `num_warps=4, num_stages=3/4` to better overlap loads; current best is likely starved on shared-memory-resident accumulators when BLOCK_SP=256 × BLOCK_OC=64 = 16K floats × stages.
- Since OC=64 fits exactly in one tile of `BLOCK_OC=64`, drop the OC-tile loop entirely and always issue one tile — removes the running-min logic and lets the compiler keep `acc` in registers.
large_guidance:
- Rewrite as an explicit im2col-style GEMM with `tl.dot`: tile is `[BLOCK_OC=64, BLOCK_SP]` accumulator built from `tl.dot(W[OC, IC*KH*KW], X_patch[IC*KH*KW, BLOCK_SP])`. With IC*KH*KW = 16*3*3 = 144, pad the K dim to 160 or 192 and loop K in `BLOCK_K=32` chunks — this replaces 144 scalar FMAs per (oc,sp) with tensor-core mma.
- Since OC=64 is small and fixed, make the kernel persistent over OC (single tile of all 64 channels) and parallelize only over `(N, spatial-tile)`. Fuse the channel-min reduction across the registers of the OC dimension before the tanh epilogue — no second pass needed.
- Consider channels-last (NHWC) input layout: reshape x to NHWC at module init / forward entry so the IC dimension is contiguous; this turns the K-axis loads into single coalesced vector loads of 16 floats per spatial position.
